channel.title: AI Stupa Translation Project
channel.description: New English translations of texts from the Tibetan Buddhist canon, made by the AI Stupa (provisional, public domain).

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Kanakavatī (Toh 924)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Kanakavatī, known in Sanskrit as Āryakanakavatīnāmadhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Pakpa Serchen Zhejawé Zung, takes its name from a word meaning "she who possesses gold." It is a dhāraṇī, a short scripture centered on a protective incantation, framed as a discourse of the Buddha. It opens with the Blessed One dwelling in an enclosure-like place together with the great yakṣa…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "Granting Fearlessness to All" (Toh 925)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "Granting Fearlessness to All," known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Sarvābhayapradāna Nāma Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phagpa Thamché La Mi Jikpa Rabtu Jinpa Zhejawé Zung, is a short scriptural dhāraṇī, a text centered on a protective incantation taught by the Buddha. It opens in the land of Magadha, where the Blessed One is staying in the rock cave of Videha, king of mountains…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "Purifying All Obstacles" (Toh 926)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "Purifying All Obstacles," known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Sarvāntarāyaviśodhanī Nāma Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phakpa Bardu Chöpa Tamché Nampar Jongwa, is a short scripture centered on a dhāraṇī, a sacred incantation believed to protect and purify those who recite it. It opens at the Indraśaila Cave on Mount Vaidehaka, north of the brahmin village of Āmraṣaṇḍā near…

item.title: The Noble King of Spells of the Drāviḍas (Toh 927)
item.description: The Noble King of Spells of the Drāviḍas, known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Drāmiḍa Vidyārāja and in Tibetan as Pakpa Drolding Wai Rikngak Kyi Gyalpo, is a short protective spell text, a dhāraṇī or vidyā, in which the Buddha offers safeguarding against the dangers of lightning. Set at Śrāvastī, it opens with the Blessed One addressing the venerable Ānanda and entrusting him with an amulet that averts…

item.title: The Noble Unconquerable One Called Giver of Fearlessness (Toh 928)
item.description: The Noble Unconquerable One Called Giver of Fearlessness, known in Sanskrit as Āryābhayapradā nāma Aparājitā, is a short dhāraṇī text centered on the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, the great being endowed with great compassion. It opens with homages to all buddhas and bodhisattvas, to the Three Jewels, and to Avalokiteśvara as the one who dispels the suffering of beings, cuts their bonds, and grants…

item.title: The Noble Unconquerable Jewel Garland (Toh 929)
item.description: The Noble Unconquerable Jewel Garland, known in Sanskrit as the Āryaratnamālā Aparājita and in Tibetan as 'Phags pa gzhan gyis mi thub pa rin po che'i phreng ba, is a short dhāraṇī text, a work centered on the recitation of protective and auspicious formulas. It opens with an extended litany of homage, first to the Three Jewels and the seventy million perfectly awakened buddhas with their…

item.title: Toh 930 (Toh 930)
item.description: This short dhāraṇī text has no title given in its opening lines, so its English, Sanskrit, and Tibetan names cannot be stated with confidence here. It begins with homage to the Three Jewels, to the Buddha Amitābha, and to the great compassionate bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara. It then presents a mantra of victory and purification, which calls on the blessing of all buddhas to cleanse the senses, the…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "Liberating from the Eight Great Fears" (Toh 931)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "Liberating from the Eight Great Fears," known in Sanskrit as the Āryāṣṭamahābhayatāraṇīnāmadhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phakpa Jikpa Chenpo Gyé Lé Drolwa Zhejawé Zung, is a short ritual text centered on a protective incantation meant to free those who recite it from the eight great fears. It opens with homage to all buddhas and bodhisattvas and then to a series of…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī of the Perfection of Wisdom in One Hundred Thousand Lines (Toh 932)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī of the Perfection of Wisdom in One Hundred Thousand Lines, whose Tibetan title begins Pakpa Sherab kyi Parol tu Chinpa, is a very short dhāraṇī text connected with the vast Perfection of Wisdom sūtra in one hundred thousand lines. After paying homage to the Blessed Mother, the Perfection of Wisdom, it presents a single Sanskrit incantation invoking the qualities of the Dharma…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī of the Noble Perfection of Wisdom in Twenty-Five Thousand Lines (Toh 933)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī of the Noble Perfection of Wisdom in Twenty-Five Thousand Lines, known in Tibetan as Phakpa Sherab kyi Parol tu Chinpa Tongtrak Nyishu Ngapé Zung and in Sanskrit, by reconstruction, as Ārya Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā Dhāraṇī, is a very brief text centered on a single incantation. It opens with homage to the Blessed Mother, the Perfection of Wisdom, and then presents a…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī of the Noble Perfection of Wisdom in Eight Thousand Lines (Toh 934)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī of the Noble Perfection of Wisdom in Eight Thousand Lines, known in Tibetan as Phakpa Sherab kyi Pharol tu Chinpa Gyaktongpé Zung and in Sanskrit approximately as Āryāṣṭasāhasrikāprajñāpāramitādhāraṇī, is a very brief work that distills one of the most celebrated Perfection of Wisdom sutras into a single incantation. After paying homage to the Blessed Mother, the Perfection of Wisdom…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī of the Essence of the Six Perfections (Toh 935)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī of the Essence of the Six Perfections, known in Tibetan as Pha rol tu phyin pa drug gi snying po'i gzungs, is a very brief incantation text whose Sanskrit title would correspond to something like a dhāraṇī of the heart or essence of the six perfections. It opens with homage to the noble Mother, the Perfection of Wisdom, and to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha. It then gives a…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī of the Vow Made by Siṃhanāda is a brief ritual incantation text (Toh 912)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī of the Vow Made by Siṃhanāda is a brief ritual incantation text, whose Sanskrit and Tibetan titles are not given in the opening lines and so are best described simply as corresponding to that English name. After an homage to Mañjughoṣa, it presents a dhāraṇī addressed to the noble Avalokiteśvara, the bodhisattva of great compassion. It then gives a short healing rite: one recites the…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī Called the Supreme Compassion (Toh 913)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī Called the Supreme Compassion, known in Sanskrit as the Karuṇāgra nāma dhāraṇī and carrying a Tibetan title of the same meaning, is a short dhāraṇī text devoted to the bodhisattva Padmapāṇi, the lotus-bearing form of Avalokiteśvara, whose wisdom is said to arise in order to rescue beings sunk in every kind of suffering. After paying homage to the Omniscient One and to Padmapāṇi, the…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Accomplishment through the Infinite Gateway (Toh 914)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Accomplishment through the Infinite Gateway, known in Sanskrit as Ārya Anantamukhasādhaka Nāma Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phakpa Go Tha Yepay Druppa Zhejawai Zung, is a dhāraṇī scripture, a text centered on a sacred formula that is recited and retained to support memory, protection, and spiritual accomplishment. Its narrative opens at Vaiśālī, in the Kūṭāgāra Hall of the…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "The Excellent Door" (Toh 915)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "The Excellent Door," known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Sumukha Nāma Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phakpa Gozangpo Zhejawé Zung, is a short scripture centered on a dhāraṇī, a sacred formula of incantation believed to carry protective and spiritual power. It opens with the familiar words "Thus did I hear at one time" and is set at the foot of the Bodhi tree, at the great shrine of…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī of the Six Gates (Toh 916)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called the Six Gates, known in Sanskrit as Ārya Ṣaṇmukha Nāma Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phakpa Go Drukpa Zhejawé Zung, is a brief dhāraṇī text that opens with homage to the youthful Mañjuśrī. Its setting is an assembly courtyard adorned with the seven precious substances and suspended in the sky above the Pure Abodes, where the Buddha, surrounded by countless bodhisattvas, urges…

item.title: The Noble Six-Syllable Vidyā-Mantra (Toh 917)
item.description: The Noble Six-Syllable Vidyā-Mantra, known in Sanskrit as Ārya Ṣaḍakṣaravidyā and in Tibetan as Pakpa Yigé Drukpé Rikngak, is a brief sūtra-style scripture centered on a protective spell. It opens at Śrāvastī, where the Buddha tells the venerable Ānanda that this "queen of six-syllable vidyā-mantras" has been proclaimed by six perfectly complete buddhas, by the four guardians of the world, and by…

item.title: The Two-Verse Dhāraṇī (Toh 918)
item.description: The Two-Verse Dhāraṇī, known in Sanskrit as the Gāthādvitīyadhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Tshigs su bcad pa gnyis pa'i gzungs, is a brief dhāraṇī text that opens with homage to the youthful Mañjuśrī. Its two verses name the obscurations that hinder sentient beings, such as contempt for the Buddha and the Dharma, laziness, complacency, desire, pride, remorse, and unsteady conduct, and they present the…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "Beautiful Bodily Form" (Toh 919)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "Beautiful Bodily Form," known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Ruciraṅgayaṣṭi nāma dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as 'Phags pa lus kyi dbyibs mdzes zhes bya ba'i gzungs, is a short dhāraṇī text. After an opening homage to all the buddhas and bodhisattvas, it consists mainly of an extended Sanskrit incantation. The incantation praises the bodhisattva Padmapāṇi, the lotus-bearing form of…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī of the Hundred Thousand Ornaments of the Essence of Awakening (Toh 920)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī of the Hundred Thousand Ornaments of the Essence of Awakening, known in Sanskrit as the Bodhigarbhālaṅkāralakṣadhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Byang chub kyi snying po'i rgyan 'bum gyi gzungs, is a short incantatory text consisting almost entirely of a single dhāraṇī, a sacred formula meant to be recited. After an opening homage to all the buddhas and bodhisattvas, the formula pays…

item.title: The Mantra and Rite by Which Building a Single Stūpa Becomes the Building of Ten Million (Toh 921)
item.description: This short work, whose Tibetan title opens with homage to the Buddha Vairocana, King of Light, and continues "de la mchod rten gcig btab na bye ba btab par 'gyur ba'i sngags dang cho ga," may be rendered in English as "The Mantra and Rite by Which Building a Single Stūpa Becomes the Building of Ten Million." No Sanskrit title is preserved in the opening lines. It is a brief ritual manual that…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "The Crest Jewel" (Toh 922)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "The Crest Jewel," known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Cūḍamaṇi Nāma Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Pakpa Tsuk gi Norbu Shejawai Zung, is a short devotional and protective text centered on the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara. It opens by paying homage to all the buddhas, bodhisattvas, śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, to the Three Jewels, and to the fully awakened buddhas of the ten…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "The Armlet on the Crest of the Banner" (Toh 923)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called "The Armlet on the Crest of the Banner," known in Sanskrit as the Āryadhvajāgrakeyūra-nāma-dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as 'Phags pa rgyal mtshan gyi rtse mo'i dpung rgyan ces bya ba'i gzungs, is a short scripture centered on a protective incantation. It opens in the Heaven of the Thirty-Three, where the Buddha is seated on a stone slab as white as wool. Śakra, lord of the…

item.title: The Essence of the Meaning of the Secret Wisdom of the Heart of All the Tathāgatas: The Sūtra of the Awareness That Gathers All the Wrathful Vajra Families, the Tantra of Accomplished Yoga, a Great Vehicle Sūtra (Toh 831)
item.description: This text is known in English as the Sūtra of the All-Gathering Awareness, or more fully the Great Vehicle Sūtra called the Essence of the Meaning of the Secret Wisdom of the Heart of All the Tathāgatas, the Sūtra of the Awareness That Gathers All the Wrathful Vajra Families, the Tantra of Accomplished Yoga; its Sanskrit title is given as Sarvatathāgatacittaguhyajñānārthagarbha…

item.title: The Tantra Called the Mirror of All Secrets (Toh 833)
item.description: The Tantra Called the Mirror of All Secrets, the Net of Magical Display of Vajrasattva, known in Sanskrit as the Vajrasattva Māyājāla Guhya Sarva Ādarśa Tantra and in Tibetan as Dorjé Sempé Gyutrul Drawa Sangwa Tamché kyi Melong, is Toh 833 in the Kangyur, where it belongs to the section of Ancient Tantras of the Nyingma school and to the Māyājāla, or Net of Magical Display, cycle of Mahāyoga…

item.title: The Secret Essence, Ascertaining Reality (Toh 834)
item.description: The Secret Essence, Ascertaining Reality, known in Sanskrit as the Guhyagarbha Tattvaviniścaya and in Tibetan as Sangwé Nyingpo De Kho Na Nyi Ngepa, is a tantra of the Net of Illusion (Māyājāla) cycle, the class of scriptures at the heart of the Ancient, or Nyingma, tradition's Mahāyoga teachings. It opens with homage to the glorious Samantabhadra and sets its scene in the boundless realm of…

item.title: The Noble Lasso of Skillful Means, the Lotus Garland (Toh 835)
item.description: The Noble Lasso of Skillful Means, the Lotus Garland, known in Tibetan as Phakpa Thabkyi Zhakpa Padmo Threng and in Sanskrit, by reconstruction, as the Ārya Upāyapāśa Padmamālā, is a tantra of the Ancient, or Nyingma, tradition, closely associated with the Guhyagarbha cycle of Mahāyoga. Framed as a dialogue in which glorious Vajrasattva, after making vast offerings, questions glorious Vairocana…

item.title: The Root Tantra of Accomplishment through Worship and Praise of the World (Toh 844)
item.description: The Root Tantra of Accomplishment through Worship and Praise of the World, known in Tibetan as Jikten Chötö Drubpa Tsawé Gyü and given a Sanskrit title that the Tibetan transmits in an irregular form beginning Lokastotrapūja Tantra, is Toh 844 in the Kangyur, where it belongs to the collection of Ancient, or Nyingma, Tantras. It is a tantra spoken by the Blessed One Vajradhara, the great secret…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī of the Ten Grounds (Toh 902)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī of the Ten Grounds, known in Sanskrit as the Daśabhūmidhāraṇī and in Tibetan by a title meaning "the dhāraṇī of the ten grounds," is a short tantric text that explains how practitioners of secret mantra can fulfill their aims. It links the single syllable oṃ to the maṇḍalas of Amoghapāśa Padmoṣṇīṣa, a form of Avalokiteśvara, the Lord of the World. It teaches that reciting the mantra a…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī of Amoghapāśa Called "Fulfilling the Six Perfections" (Toh 903)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī of Amoghapāśa Called "Fulfilling the Six Perfections," known in Sanskrit as Ārya Amoghapāśa Pāramitā Ṣaṭparipūraka Nāma Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phagpa Dönyö Zhakpé Pharol Tu Chinpa Drug Yongsu Dzokpar Jepa Zhejawé Zung, is a short dhāraṇī text centered on Amoghapāśa, the form of the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara whose name means "Unfailing Noose." After paying homage to all the…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Samantabhadra (Toh 904)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Samantabhadra, known in Sanskrit as Ārya Samantabhadra Nāma Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phakpa Kuntu Zangpo Zhejawé Zung, is a short scripture centered on a dhāraṇī, a sacred incantation believed to carry protective and spiritually transformative power. It opens on Vulture Peak near Rājagṛha, where the Buddha is teaching before a vast gathering of monks, bodhisattvas, and…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Nīlakaṇṭha (Toh 905)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Nīlakaṇṭha, known in Sanskrit as Āryanīlakaṇṭhanāmadhāraṇī and in Tibetan as 'Phags pa nī la kaṇ ṭha zhes bya ba'i gzungs, is a short dhāraṇī text devoted to Avalokiteśvara, the bodhisattva of compassion, here invoked under the name Nīlakaṇṭha, meaning "blue-throated." After paying homage to the Three Jewels, to the Buddha Amitābha, and to the bodhisattva…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī of Avalokiteśvara Hayagrīva (Toh 906)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī of Avalokiteśvara Hayagrīva, known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Avalokiteśvara Hayagrīva Dhāraṇī and in Tibetan by a title that opens with "Phakpa Chenrezik," the Noble Avalokiteśvara, is a short incantatory text devoted to Hayagrīva, the horse-necked wrathful form associated with the bodhisattva of compassion. After paying homage to all buddhas and bodhisattvas, it presents a long…

item.title: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Mekhalā (Toh 907)
item.description: The Noble Dhāraṇī Called Mekhalā, known in Sanskrit as the Ārya Mekhalā Nāma Dhāraṇī and carrying a Tibetan title of the same meaning, is a short protective scripture centered on a spell, or vidyā-mantra, named Mekhalā. It opens in the Nyagrodha park near Kapilavastu, in the land of the Śākyas, where the young Rāhula, the Buddha's son, comes weeping to the Blessed One after being terrified in the…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī Called "Compassion Without Delay" (Toh 908)
item.description: Compassion Without Delay, known in Tibetan as Snying rjes mi bshol ba, is a short dhāraṇī devoted to the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, the great being renowned for his boundless compassion. It opens with homage to the Three Jewels, to seventy million perfect buddhas, and to Avalokiteśvara as the one who frees beings from harm, pacifies illness, turns back hostile spirits, and rescues those caught…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī Called "Mother of Noble Avalokiteśvara" (Toh 909)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī Called "Mother of Noble Avalokiteśvara," known in Sanskrit as Āryāvalokiteśvaramātā nāma dhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phakpa Chenrezik Wangchuk gi Yum zhe jawé Zung, is a short scripture centered on a dhāraṇī, an incantation held to preserve and empower those who recite it. It opens in the city of Vaiśālī, where the Buddha is seated amid a great assembly of five hundred monks, among them…

item.title: The Dhāraṇī of Noble Avalokiteśvara (Toh 910)
item.description: The Dhāraṇī of Noble Avalokiteśvara, known in Sanskrit as Āryāvalokiteśvaranāmadhāraṇī and in Tibetan as Phakpa Chenrezik Wangchuk gi Zung, is a short devotional and meditative work dedicated to Avalokiteśvara, the bodhisattva of great compassion. After an opening homage, it guides the practitioner through a visualization in which Avalokiteśvara, moved by loving-kindness and compassion, arises…

item.title: The Heart of Noble Avalokiteśvara (Toh 911)
item.description: The Heart of Noble Avalokiteśvara, known in Tibetan as Phakpa Chenrezik kyi Nyingpo and likely corresponding to a Sanskrit title along the lines of Ārya Avalokiteśvara Hṛdaya, is a very brief devotional text centered on a single knowledge mantra. It opens with homage to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, and to the noble bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, the great being. It then presents a mantra…

item.title: Praise of the Subduer of Māra (Toh 1117)
item.description: The Praise of the Subduer of Māra, in Tibetan Dü Tulwa la Töpa, is a brief hymn whose Tibetan version gives no Sanskrit title. In three long verses it celebrates the Buddha's victory over Māra on the eve of his awakening: the jealous women of Māra taunt him for a meditation they call false and heartless, Kāma and the hosts of Māra with their bows, drums and animal-faced warriors fail to shake his…

item.title: Praise to the Dharmadhātu (Toh 1118)
item.description: The Praise to the Dharmadhātu, known in Sanskrit as the Dharmadhātustava and in Tibetan as Chökyi Ying su Töpa, is a hymn in verse that its colophon attributes to the great master Nāgārjuna, translated into Tibetan by the Indian preceptor Kṛṣṇa Paṇḍita and the translator Tsultrim Gyalwa. It praises the dharmadhātu, the basic nature of reality present in every sentient being, which, while veiled…

item.title: Praise to the Incomparable One (Toh 1119)
item.description: The Praise to the Incomparable One, known in Sanskrit as the Niraupamyastava and in Tibetan as Pemé Par Töpa, is a short hymn in verse attributed to the master Nāgārjuna and traditionally counted among his collected praises of the Buddha. Opening with homage to the youthful Mañjuśrī, it lauds the Buddha as one who knows the absence of entities, who found peace not by abandoning saṃsāra but by not…

item.title: Praise to the One Who Transcends the World (Toh 1120)
item.description: The Praise to the One Who Transcends the World, known in Sanskrit as the Lokātītastava and in Tibetan as Jikten Lé Dépar Töpa, is a hymn in verse attributed to the master Nāgārjuna and traditionally counted among his collected praises of the Buddha. Addressing the Buddha as one who has gone beyond the world yet labors tirelessly for beings out of compassion, it praises his teaching through a…

item.title: Praise of the Vajra of Mind (Toh 1121)
item.description: The Praise of the Vajra of Mind, in Sanskrit Cittavajrastava and in Tibetan Semkyi Dorjé Töpa, is a brief hymn of seven verses that its colophon attributes to the master Nāgārjuna. Opening with homage to Mañjuśrī, it praises one's own mind as the true object of devotion, teaching that awakening is the realization of mind, that the five destinies and all happiness and suffering are nothing apart…

item.title: Praise of the Ultimate (Toh 1122)
item.description: Praise of the Ultimate, known in Sanskrit as the Paramārthastava and in Tibetan as Döndampar Töpa, is a short hymn in verse attributed to the master Nāgārjuna and traditionally counted among his Four Hymns (Catuḥstava). It praises the Buddha from the standpoint of ultimate truth by way of negation: the Protector is unborn and without abode, neither an entity nor a non-entity, beyond color, shape…

item.title: Praise of the Three Bodies (Toh 1123)
item.description: The Praise of the Three Bodies, known in Sanskrit as the Kāyatrayastotra and in Tibetan as Kusum la Töpa, is a brief hymn of four verses honoring the three bodies of the buddhas. After an opening homage to the youthful Mañjuśrī, it praises in turn the truth body (dharmakāya), which is neither one nor many, neither an entity nor a nonentity, and is known through each one's own direct awareness…

item.title: A Commentary on the Praise of the Three Bodies (Toh 1124)
item.description: This is A Commentary on the Praise of the Three Bodies, known in Sanskrit as the Kāyatrayastotranāmasyavivaraṇa and in Tibetan as Kusum la Töpa Zhé Jawé Nampar Drelpa. It is a phrase-by-phrase explanation of Nāgārjuna's short hymn, the Praise of the Three Bodies, which pays homage in turn to the three bodies of a buddha: the Dharma body, beyond one and many and beyond existence and nonexistence…

item.title: Praise for Pleasing Sentient Beings (Toh 1125)
item.description: The Praise for Pleasing Sentient Beings, known in Sanskrit as the Sattvārādhanastava and in Tibetan as Semchen Gupar Jawé Töpa, is a short hymn of eleven verses in which the Buddha himself is the speaker. Its single theme is that the true way to revere the Buddha and make offering to him is to benefit sentient beings: whoever harms beings harms him, even a small kindness to them is an offering…

item.title: Praise of the Great Vajradhara (Toh 1126)
item.description: Praise of the Great Vajradhara, known in Sanskrit as the Mahāvajradharastotra and in Tibetan as Dorjé Chang Chenpö Töpa, is a short hymn in verse presented as the words of the great bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, who praises the Blessed One, the great Vajradhara, with what the text calls a king of praises. Its eight stanzas hail Vajradhara as the inseparability of the conventional and ultimate truths, as…

item.title: Praise of the Perfection of Wisdom (Toh 1127)
item.description: Praise of the Perfection of Wisdom, known in Sanskrit as the Prajñāpāramitāstotra and in Tibetan as Sherab kyi Pharol tu Chinmé Töpa, is a hymn in verse addressed to the Perfection of Wisdom as a feminine presence, the Blessed Lady, who is as inseparable from the buddhas as moonlight is from the moon. Over some twenty verses it praises her as stainless and beyond words, the loving mother of the…
